channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Drake Maye completed 16-of-20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ 24-19, Week 8 win over the Dolphins, adding eight rushes for five yards and one touchdown.
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

Maye’s two-yard touchdown run was a thing of beauty. The Patriots quarterback took off to the right side of the field, faking a pitch to Rhamondre Stevenson, which caused a Dolphins defender to fully bite on it, running right past Maye while the Patriots’ quarterback darted into the end zone. Maye’s first touchdown pass was thrown to Kyle Williams on a post route. It was well-placed, allowing Williams to secure the ball in stride just before entering the end zone. Maye later linked up with DeMario Douglas via play action for his second score. The Patriots’ quarterback is a QB1 against the Packers next week.

item.title: Emmett Johnson caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Emmett Johnson KC Running Back

He added one carry for 15 yards. Johnson racked up the bulk of his production on a 73-yard touchdown grab in the first half. The Broncos sent pressure and Patrick Mahomes perfectly lofted the ball to Johnson, who saw nothing but green grass ahead of him. The turf monster nearly took him down at the 10-yard line, but Johnson stayed upright enough and lost one final defender on his way into the end zone. He also picked up a 38-yard catch just before halftime to set up a last-second field goal. Johnson had more than two touches in just one of his previous three games headed into Week 8. Though he’s not going to challenge Kenneth Walker for RB1 duties anytime soon, this breakout performance should earn him a few more touches in Week 9. He will be have some value as a boom/bust FLEX play versus the Jets.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes completed 30-of-41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 28-24, Week 8 loss to the Broncos.
item.description:
Patrick Mahomes KC Quarterback

Mahomes posted a strong box score for fantasy managers and took care of the football with zero turnovers. He also took just two sacks, but the second was one that will haunt Chiefs fans for a while. After marching the offense down to the goal line under the two-minute warning, the Chiefs found themselves on fourth-and-goal. They initially got the score via a strike to Rashee Rice, but the play was blown dead via a false start. The Broncos’ pass-rush got to him on the second try, taking Mahomes down for a game-ending sack. On the whole, it was another dink-and-dunk game plan from Mahomes, who failed to get the deep ball going once again. Luckily for him, Emmet Johnson averaged 25.6 yards per catch and turned a short toss into a 73-yard touchdown in the first half. The Chiefs get a bounce-back spot against the Jets next week in a game where Mahomes will be just inside the QB1 ranks.

item.title: Kyren Willliams had 16 rushes for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers, adding one catch for three yards.
item.description:
Kyren Williams

The more efficient Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and did not see a target in a run-heavy Rams offense. Williams led the LA backfield in routes but only had one look from Matthew Stafford. He was stuffed at the line of scrimmage a handful of times in the first half. The rushing volume in the Rams offense of late should make both Williams and Coum fantasy relevant every week, including next week against the Commanders.

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said OC Mike McDaniel will continue to call plays after the team’s 9-24, Week 8 loss to the Rams.
item.description:
Mike McDaniel LAC Offensive Coordinator

Harbaugh is standing by the organization’s biggest offseason hire. The Chargers at least got a little passing production going today, though obviously the results continue to fall short of expectations. The Chargers, now 0-6, face the Texans, 2-5, in Week 9. Houston’s underperforming defense could give the Chargers a chance to improve their standing next week.

Source: Fernando Ramirez

item.title: Puka Nacua caught 11-of-12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Nacua, with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, again dominated targets in the newly run-heavy LA offense. No other Rams pass catcher saw more than four targets on the day. Nacua’s touchdown came on a well-designed screen in the second half at the end of a long drive for the run-first Rams offense. Nacua, who had 41 targets over his prior four games, is among the safest players in fantasy football. He matches up against the Commanders in Week 9.

item.title: Tyler Higbee caught 1-of-2 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Tyler Higbee

It was another disappointing outing for Higbee. This one came with Colby Parkinson (ribs) sidelined. Davis Allen had two catchers on two targets for eight yards. Higbee now hasn’t had more than 25 yards receiving in a game since the beginning of October, and has lost opportunities with the Rams going run heavy in recent weeks. Higbee won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Commanders.

item.title: Jack Campbell (neck) will remain in a local hospital tonight for continued evaluation and monitoring.
item.description:
Jack Campbell DET Linebacker

This update comes straight from the Lions’ organization. Campbell was taken to a local hospital shortly after being taken off the field on a stretcher. He is reportedly resting now. The team will provide further updates as it has them. We hope he recovers quickly and completely.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Jalen Nailor caught 4-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Jalen Nailor LV Wide Receiver

Nailor’s touchdown was his first as a Raider. It went down for all of two yards. In addition to the score, Nailor posted new season highs in yards and receptions, which obviously tells you all you need to know about his WR4 value: He doesn’t have any heading into Week 9 against the 49ers.

item.title: Michael Mayer caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Michael Mayer LV Tight End

This was Mayer’s fourth five-catch outing of the season. Only Brock Bowers caught more passes this afternoon. It could have been a bigger day in fantasy, but Mayer’s unconverted look was an inaccurate goal-line pass he short-armed. Mayer has a reasonable enough PPR TE2 floor, but his spiked week potential remains limited enough that he is not a very exciting streamer.

item.title: Blake Corum had 11 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers.
item.description:
Blake Corum

Kyren Williams led the LA backfield with 16 carries for 56 yards. Corum was much more efficient as a rusher against the Chargers, regularly bursting through the line of scrimmage and shedding tacklers on a couple second half runs. The Rams have been run heavy since Davante Adams went down with a serious hamstring injury a few weeks ago. That’s generated more opportunity for Corum, who last week had 17 rushes. He ranks 44th among running backs in expected fantasy points per game in 2026. That kind of usage should make Corum flex-viable for now. He gets the Commanders in Week 9.

item.title: Tre Tucker was held without a catch in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Tre Tucker LV Wide Receiver

Coming off 10/200/3 over the past two weeks, Tucker somehow commanded only one target in a game where the Raiders scored 38 points. It was the first time since the opener he caught fewer than four passes. Tucker has definitely benefitted from some garbage time production, but he is not typically going to be a zero waiting to happen. He can still be trotted out there as a low-end WR3 for a Week 9 matchup where the Raiders are going to have to pass to compete with the 49ers.

item.title: Seth McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Seth McGowan IND Running Back

McGowan actually out-gained Jonathan Taylor on the ground in a game the Colts trailed 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 heading into the fourth quarter. No. 3 back DJ Giddens was called upon for six carries, which he turned into 43 yards. Fantasy managers are stuck in a holding pattern as they await Taylor’s Colts fate ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but McGowan remains worth a speculative stash in most 12-team leagues.

item.title: Justin Herbert completed 24-of-32 attempts for 257 yards and two interceptions in the Chargers’ Week 8 loss to the Rams, adding four rushes for 15 yards.
item.description:
Justin Herbert LAC Quarterback

Coming off their bye week, the Chargers looked worse than ever on offense, with Herbert apparently confused as to where to throw the ball or how to conduct OC Mike McDaniel’s complex pre-snap motion scheme. Herbert had a negative EPA per drop back. Both of his picks were of the mind blogging variety, thrown directly to Rams defenders in the open field. Frustrated and dejected, Herbert continues his worst pro season for the winless Bolts. As usual, Herbert — who ranks 33rd in fantasy points per game — won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Texans.

item.title: Keenan Allen caught 7-of-7 targets for 67 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Keenan Allen IND Wide Receiver

As is now the case every week, Allen easily lead the Colts in most every receiving category. That did not include targets — a returning Tyler Warren commanded 10 looks — but Allen out-gained him 67-18. Now Allen and fantasy managers must sit and wait to see what kind of moves the tanking Colts make ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. That could include non-roster changes like the benching of Daniel Jones. For now a low-end WR3, Allen could be valued much differently 10 days from now.

item.title: Josh Downs caught 4-of-5 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Downs’ score was something of a pity touchdown in a game the Colts were trailing 35-0 at the 3:59 mark of the third quarter. Jacksonville’s defense had a rare mixup, and Downs was roaming free in the end zone. Amazingly, it was his first touchdown of the year. That speaks to just how dire things have been for Downs in an offense with an ineffective Daniel Jones and ageless Keenan Allen. Downs, who of course must be held responsible for his own mediocre play, will have no shot at a 2026 fantasy revival unless he’s subject to a change-of-scenery trade ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

item.title: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, LB Jihaad Campbell, WR Dontayvion Wicks, CB Jonathan Jones, OL Jake Majors , and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 8 against the Commanders.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

The Eagles continue to trudge on without key contributors as they enter Week 8 down their top two wide receivers and starting quarterback. Running back Saquon Barkley is active after being removed from the injury report Friday, with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue on hand for change of pace duties. Covey’s absence is primarily a hit to the Philadelphia special teams unit, who will continue to require alternate contributions to kick returns.

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) is active for Week 8 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

The team’s Week 7 bye apparently afforded Burks enough time to overcome the foot injury sustained late in the fourth quarter of Washington’s Week 6 loss, confirming previous reports that indicated Burks would be active after entering the weekend listed as questionable. Expect Burks to operate as a starter alongside veteran Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams, the latter two of whom carry greater upside against the inside-funnel Philadelphia defense. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, G Tanoa Togiai, DT Daron Payne, and DT Javon Kinlaw.

item.title: Mike Washington rushed 25 times for 83 yards in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

At least for one week, the Raiders formalized Washington’s early-down takeover, as the rookie out-carried a doghoused Ashton Jeanty 25-2. However, Washington got routinely stood up on his ample goal-line opportunities, and only out-gained Jeanty 83-73 thanks to Jeanty’s involvement in the passing game. A 45-yard reception where Jeanty literally fell down to catch an inaccurate Kirk Cousins pass only to get up and rumble nearly half the length of the field was by far the biggest play by a Raiders running back in this one. Although Washington now has to be considered the favorite for early-down work, he was uninspiring enough this afternoon that it’s not going to be an open-and-shut case against the 49ers. We would still rather start Jeanty in fantasy because of his pass catching.

item.title: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Taylor’s five targets were third on the team behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, while fellow seam stretcher Kenyon Sadiq mustered only two looks. Taylor has become a weekly volume presence in an offense that attempts a lot of passes, but he has not established a particularly high floor while his spiked week odds remain practically nonexistent. He’s a TE2 by the letter of the law but not one we would be looking to start in Week 9 against the Chiefs.

item.title: Kenyon Sadiq caught a 22-yard pass in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
item.description:
Kenyon Sadiq NYJ Tight End

Sadiq’s third quarter reception went down as one of just two targets for the rookie tight end. He was once again out-caught by Mason Taylor, though Taylor provided just 19 yards across his three grabs. Sadiq’s reception was an impressive, leaping catch against single coverage, but therein lies part of the problem: It’s taking spectacular acts for Sadiq to create fantasy value. He is sadly off the radar for the time being in 12-team leagues.

item.title: Broncos S Brandon Jones suffered a hamstring injury and will not return in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Brandon Jones DEN Safety

With Talanoa Hufanga also sidelined heading into this game, both of Denver’s starting safeties from Week 8 are out. Luckily for Denver, Pat Surtani is back this week, giving them some extra firepower in their secondary. Jones has two interceptions and five pass breakups this year.

item.title: Jake Bates made two of his three field goal attempts in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jake Bates DET Kicker

Bates boinked one off the uprights in the second half, his first field goal miss of the 2026 season. One of the most reliable kickers in the NFL, Bates doesn’t get much opportunity thanks largely to Dan Campbell’s fourth down aggressiveness. Bates, who has just one game with multiple field goal tries this year, will be an iffy option in Week 9 against the Dolphins.

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) was taken back to the locker room after briefly returning in Week 8 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry briefly returned to the sideline after halftime, where he tested out his injured left foot. Evidently, the sideline testing did not go well. Henry was then taken right back to the locker room by the Patriots’ training staff. If the Patriots do end up ruling him out, as we expect, he will finish the day having caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards.

item.title: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-12 targets for 83 yards in the Jets’ Week 8 loss to the Raiders.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Fresh off a three-target fiasco that prompted trade request denials from the Jets’ No. 1 wideout, Wilson was jammed the ball early and often. It was a clear, intentional commitment from Geno Smith and the Jets’ coaching staff. It still couldn’t prevent Wilson from once again getting out-shined by one of his positional mates, this time Adonai Mitchell. AD contributed an explosive 7/142/1 on nine looks. That’s now three 100-yard performances by Jets wideouts over the past three weeks with zero of them coming from Wilson. He still commands the most defensive attention, making life easier for Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Despite those frustrations and Wilson’s relative struggles, he will remain a must start for Week 9 against the Chiefs.

item.title: Brock Bowers caught 7-of-10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 8 win over the Jets.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

The multi-score start was Bowers’ first of the season but third of his career. He won a first quarter end zone hand fight for a 12-yarder before later contributing a two-yarder where he broke some tackles. He is now up to five touchdowns in six games and has yet to finish below 70 yards. That is league-winning type stuff out of the tight end position. The 49ers are on deck as a tough matchup up the seam for Week 9.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts, adding a 17-yard reception.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez was still getting out-snapped and out-produced by a percolating Bhayshul Tuten, but he managed to contribute a 28-yard score in a blowout victory. Rodriguez hit the hole then emerged to an abandoned mall of a Colts defense. With the Jaguars heading on the road for a short-week Thursday night date with a Ravens team operating without Lamar Jackson, expect lots of “get me out of here” Jags rushes in Baltimore, locking Rodriguez in as a Week 9 FLEX play.

item.title: Gunnar Helm caught 5-of-9 targets for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Gunnar Helm TEN Tight End

Helm saw career-highs in targets and receiving yards in a high-scoring game against the Bengals. He saw a few targets in the flats but was targeted downfield multiple times, catching two passes of at least 24 yards. Helm also caught a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter. He is the Titans primary pass-catching tight end and saw heavy usage in a pass-heavy game script. Fantasy managers should not anticipate more game scripts like this for the Titans but Helm is a deep league streaming tight end option once the Titans come out of a Week 9 bye week.

item.title: Isaac TeSlaa did not have a catch in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
item.description:
Isaac TeSlaa DET Wide Receiver

TeSlaa has been effectively phased out of the Detroit passing attack. he has one catch over his past three games, and against the Vikings on Sunday he ran 13 routes on 35 Lions drop backs and did not see a target. He can be dropped in most formats.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange had a 46-yard first quarter catch-and-run that went down as the Jags’ longest gain of the day in a 42-7 demolition of the pathetic Colts. Strange was really rumbling, looking out of gas at the end of his journey. Strange actually tied for the team lead in receiving yards, but that’s because Trevor Lawrence attempted all of 14 passes. Strange has done enough to keep himself in the TE2 mix, but he is not an ideal TE1 streamer heading into a short-week Thursday night date vs. a Ravens team that will be without Lamar Jackson.

item.title: Chase McLaughlin converted 3-of-3 field goal attempts in the Bucs’ Week 8 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Chase McLaughlin TB Kicker

McLaughlin also nailed his only PAT try. The Bucs forced a trio of turnovers in the first half. Their ensuring drives didn’t amount to much, but the field position alone allowed McLaughlin to put the ball through the uprights on two of them. With the Faclons accomplishing nothing on offense, the Bucs were comfortable taking the points throughout the contest, resulting in another strong fantasy outing for McLaughlin. He entered Week 8 as a top five fantasy option and will remain near the top of the kicker ranks for Week 9 versus the Bears.

item.title: Travis Hunter was held without a catch in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Travis Hunter

Hunter did add a five-yard “rush” on what sure looked like a pass attempt from Trevor Lawrence, but that’s neither her nor there. What is here is a rather predictable letdown after Hunter went into the Jaguars’ Week 7 bye with a pop-up effort in London. Although it was good to see Hunter contribute at all on offense, his role is too limited in an attack with too many mouths to feed to treat him as even a boom/bust WR4. That includes for Thursday’s short-week date with a Ravens team now missing starting quarterback Lamar Jackson.

item.title: Chimere Dike caught 5-of-6 targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Chimere Dike TEN Wide Receiver

Dike saw 58 snaps with Carnell Tate out, second among Titans wide receivers. He scored on an 11-yard reception in the fourth quarter. It was Dike’s first game with over three receptions and second game over one target this season. Dike is mostly utilized as a kick returner but is in line to see increased opportunities on offense if Tate misses additional time. For now, Dike should be off the fantasy radar heading into the Titans’ Week 9 bye.

item.title: Wan’Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 57 yards, a touchdown and a fumble in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals.
item.description:
Wan'Dale Robinson TEN Wide Receiver

Robinson led Titans wide receivers in targets and snaps with Carnell Tate out, seeing seven targets. He was involved in his usual short-yardage role out of the slot, averaging 9.5 yards per reception with a 15-yard fourth quarter touchdown boosting his fantasy production. He was credited with a fumble on a screen pass that controversially could have been ruled an incomplete pass. Robinson is consistently a checkdown target for Cam Ward, with intermediate targets sparsely sprinkled in. Tate may return out of the Titans’ Week 9 bye, leaving Robinson to fend for fantasy production in the fantasy WR4 ranks.

item.title: Sione Vaki had 11 rushes for 65 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding one catch for five yards.
item.description:
Sione Vaki DET Running Back

It was the first time this year Vaki has seen more than six carries. The Lions went ultra run-heavy in this one to combat the Vikings’ vexing blitz scheme, which led to 35 carries on the day. Vaki should be stashed in most formats in cae Jahmyr Gibbs misses any time in the coming weeks. Vaki would be a potential 20-touch weekly option in such a scenario.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers wasn’t the only Jags pass catcher to post an empty box score in a 42-7 obliteration where Trevor Lawrence attempted only 14 passes, though he’s now been held to two or fewer receptions in 4-of-7 games. For a supposed “floor” player, that is not going to cut it, especially since Meyers is not the ceiling threat in this offense. With volume likely to remain in short supply for Thursday’s short-week tilt with the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens, Meyers is not a compelling WR3 for Week 9.

item.title: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-5 targets for 95 yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
item.description:
Jahan Dotson ATL Wide Receiver

The bulk of Dotson’s production came on a single, 76-yard gain in the fourth quarter. Michael Penix lobbed him a ball on the boundary and two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson uncovered with room to run. He bolted down the sideline but didn’t have the speed to take it to the house. That play alone accounted for over half of Penix’s passing output. Dotson has made the occasional splash play while running as Atlanta’s WR2, but his fantasy prospects are not that intriguing headed into Week 9. He will be in the WR5/6 range when the Falcons take on the Bengals next week.

item.title: Brian Thomas Jr. scored a 12-yard touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Thomas’ first quarter score — only his second of the season — was one of just two looks in a game where Trevor Lawrence attempted all of 14 passes against an overmatched Colts squad. He got lost behind the final Colts defender in the end zone and hauled in a dime from T-Law. Now the question becomes if he ever catches another pass in Jacksonville. With the Jags’ final game before the Nov. 10 trade deadline coming this Thursday night against the Ravens, Thomas probably will suit up for Week 9. With the Jags being highly unlikely to open up their passing attack vs. a Ravens side now down to its No. 2 or 3 quarterback, Thomas must remain glued to 12-team league benches.

item.title: Aaron Jones had five rushes for 22 yards in the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions, adding two catches for 18 yards.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jordan Mason led the Minnesota backfield with eight rushes (for 20 yards) while Jones remained the team’s preferred pass-catching option out of the backfield. Jones was battling a knee injury headed into the game and did not appear to be 100 percent against Detroit. He’ll be a deep league flex option in Week 9 against the Bills.

item.title: Kyle Pitts caught 2-of-5 targets for six yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
item.description:
Kyle Pitts ATL Tight End

Pitts’ 20 percent target share would have been good for at least TE2 fantasy numbers on a normal day. This game was anything but normal. Pitts and Jahan Dotson were the only Falcons pass-catchers with multiple receptions. Michael Penix only completed eight passes, so there simply wasn’t enough production to go around. He was intercepted four times and the Falcons were shut out. Pitts role as a PPR merchant should tick back up in Week 9 versus the Bengals. He will be back in the TE2 mix for that contest.

item.title: Tony Pollard rushed 21 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 8 loss to the Bengals, adding three receptions for 20 yards.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Pollard had his second-straight multi-touchdown game, scoring the first touchdown of the game on a 40-yard scamper with multiple missed tackles and a stiff-arm in the first quarter. With Tyjae Spears out, Pollard was the only Titans running back that got touches. He recovered his own fumble in the second half and added a one-yard score in the third quarter. He was also dropped for a safety in the third quarter on a head-scratching delayed hand-off to give the Bengals two points. Pollard enters the Titans’ Week 9 bye with several trade rumors swirling; if he is still in Tennessee, Pollard is a fantasy RB2 for Week 10.

item.title: Tyler Warren caught 4-of-10 targets for 18 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren was active for the first time since Week 5 after recovering from a groin injury. As if that inefficiency was not enough, Warren also batted a late second quarter target into the air for an “interception” that turned into a 92-yard Jaguars touchdown. Brutal stuff, not that it’s anything new in a season where Warren has only two touchdowns and is averaging an abysmal 6.8 yards per reception. Daniel Jones is not playing well, but his seemingly inevitable benching would only make things worse with Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard as the “alternatives.” Warren will be a low-end TE1 for Week 9 against the Cowboys. That is at least an A+ matchup.

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught 7-of-8 targets for 46 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown added ten yards on a carry, which was actually a running catch on a play in which St. Brown lined up fifteen yards behind the line of scrimmage and got a running start like you might see in the CFL. He had a touchdown catch called back in the first half and had to go to the locker room with what looked to be a knee issue. It was only the second time this season St. Brown was held to less than 60 yards. He came into Week 8 ranked fourth in expected fantasy points per game. St. Brown takes on the Bills in Week 9.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards in the Colts’ Week 8 loss to the Jaguars, adding four receptions for 24 yards.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

With the Colts losing 28-0 at halftime and 42-7 going into the fourth quarter, there simply wasn’t any run to be established. Daniel Jones also short-circuited two drives with interceptions, further limiting volume in a game where it was already exceedingly difficult to come by. You could question why Taylor even played at all as trade rumors swirl ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, but that will be a bigger question mark in Week 9 against the Cowboys. That’s a far better matchup than the Jaguars, so even if Taylor remains in limbo, you will have no choice but to fire him up for what could be his final game in a Colts uniform.

item.title: Jack Endries caught his sole target for one yard and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Jack Endries CIN Tight End

Endries got his first career catch and touchdown at the goal line in the second quarter against the Titans. The 22-year-old saw 11 snaps, getting a few increased opportunities with Tanner Hudson hitting injured reserve a few weeks ago. Endries should not be rostered for fantasy purposes, but enters the scene with his first career touchdown in a win over the Titans.

item.title: Mike Gesicki caught 4-of-6 targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Mike Gesicki CIN Tight End

Gesicki has been a high-value red zone target for the Bengals all season long. His score against the Titans came from outside of the red zone, catching a 25-yard pass for the score in the fourth quarter. It’s Gesicki’s sixth-straight game with a touchdown and seventh score of the season. Pass-heavy game scripts will lift all boats in the Bengals offense but Gesicki remains a high-end fantasy TE2 due to his high amount of touchdown opportunities.

item.title: Justice Hill rushed three times for 15 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 20 yards on eight targets.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Hill nearly turned into a surprise PPR scam this week with rookie UDFA Joe Fagnano under center for two-and-a-half quarters of play. Hill’s eight targets led all Ravens players, but his 20 receiving yards were largely buoyed by back-to-back receptions during a two-minute drill when the Ravens were facing second and third and longs. Despite the high-volume day, it’s hard to rely on anybody in this offense, which could have dark days ahead with Lamar Jackson (thumb) out for the foreseeable future and Tyler Huntley also dealing with a toe injury.

item.title: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-5 targets for 33 yards in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

LaPorta had a quiet day against a Minnesota defense that has shut down opposing tight ends for much of the season. He had at least 80 receiving yards in each of that past two Detroit games. LaPorta had been a serviceable starting tight end headed into Week 8, and should have a better outlook in Week 9 against the Bills. He’s been targeted on 18 percent of his routes on the season.

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 10-of-11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins led the team in receiving yards while trailing Ja’Marr Chase in receptions and targets. He was Joe Burrow’s primary target over the middle of the field in the intermediate and deep areas. Higgins caught a pair of second half touchdowns, catching an 18-yard score to tie the game towards the end of regulation. Pass-heavy game scripts will lead to a high amount of fantasy production for Higgins and Chase, who saw a combined 56-percent target share from Joe Burrow. Higgins is a high-end WR2 for Week 9 against the Falcons.

item.title: Drake London caught 1-of-6 targets for eight yards in the Falcons’ Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
item.description:
Drake London ATL Wide Receiver

Bucs defenders caught more passes on London’s six targets than he did. It was that bad of a day. Michael Penix was intercepted four times and only completed eight attempts. He managed just 125 yards, over half of which came on a 76-yard throw to Jahan Dotson that was the result of a coverage miscue. There’s simply not much to take away from a game where London’s quarterback plays this poorly. London had gone for at least 60 yards on four catches in every previous Penix start. We fully expect him to get back on track as a WR1 versus the Bengals next week.

item.title: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-4 targets for 14 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

It was another day at the office for Andrews, who has now gone six straight games with 28 or fewer receiving yards. Any hope that he might see a slight increase in production with Lamar Jackson back under center can be put aside after Jackson suffered a severe injury to his throwing hand that will require surgery and force him to go on injured reserve. Andrews isn’t on the fantasy radar heading into Week 9 against the Jaguars.

item.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught 4-of-5 targets for 31 yards in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to Arizona.
item.description:
Brevyn Spann-Ford DAL Tight End

With Jake Ferguson (ankle) felled early, Spann-Ford played 65-of-74 snaps for the Cowboys and was second on the team in targets as Dallas tried to find a solution for the blitz. Spann-Ford would likely factor into the TE2 ranks next week if Ferguson were unable to play.

item.title: Jameson Williams caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings.
item.description:
Jameson Williams DET Wide Receiver

Williams scored the Lions’ lone passing touchdown on a short corner-of-the-end-zone grab in the first half. Williams was second behind Amon-Ra St. Brown in targets, functioning as the primary downfield threat with a nice 46-yard catch on a Jared Goff shot down the middle. Williams, who came into Week 8 with the 16th most air yards among wide receivers this season, should remain in lineups next week against a vulnerable Buffalo secondary that has struggled against boundary wideouts.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 11-of-16 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 8 win over the Titans.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase was heavily involved in a pass-heavy game script, seeing 16-of-48 Joe Burrow pass attempts. He was targeted downfield several times, catching a 30-yard touchdown but being the intended target on a pair of interceptions. It was Chase’s first 100-yard receiving day as he led the team in targets and receptions. The Bengals have a pass funnel to Chase and Tee Higgins, leading to extremely productive fantasy days in high scoring games. Chase is once again squarely in the fantasy WR1 ranks for Week 9 against the Falcons.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 8 win over the Colts, adding two receptions for 55 yards and a second score.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

It was a red letter day for the second-year pro, who: 1. Posted a new career high in rushing. 2. Posted a new career high in receiving. 3. Posted just his second two-touchdown outing. No. 3 is perhaps the most notable since Tuten’s first two-score day came heading into the Jags’ Week 7 bye. Tuten is taking off in fantasy even as Chris Rodriguez Jr. remains involved. It’s due in part to the fact that the Jags are dominating game script and dictating tempo, but Tuten is also just genuinely running well. Today that included even after he had to get an ankle taped. That will be something to monitor heading into Thursday’s short-week date with the Ravens, but Tuten should be good to go as a high-end RB2.

item.title: Ja’Kobi Lane caught his lone target for 13 yards in the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills.
item.description:
Ja'Kobi Lane BAL Wide Receiver

Lane hauled in a 13-yard reception from Joe Fagnano in the second quarter after Fagnano came in to replace Tyler Huntley (toe). Lane has yet to live up to the training camp hype he drew all offseason and seems even less likely to hit his stride with Lamar Jackson’s (thumb) in jeopardy. Fantasy managers stashing Lane in deeper leagues can move to drop him at this time.

item.title: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 8 loss to the Cardinals.
item.description:
Ryan Flournoy DAL Wide Receiver

He added a DPI at the two-yard line to set up another score, and dropped another pass in the red zone. It’s clear that he’s cutting into George Pickens’ production at this point; Flournoy has gone over 90 yards or scored in three of his last four starts. He’ll be a reasonable FLEX play next week against the Colts, although the Cowboys may abandon the pass at some point in that one.

item.title: Michael Penix completed 8-of-24 passes for 125 yards and four interceptions in the Falcons’ 16-0, Week 8 loss to the Bucs.
item.description:
Michael Penix ATL Quarterback

Penix got off to a poor start and his play spiraled from there. He threw a pass directly at Bucs linebacker Alex Anzalone’s chest on the first play of Atlanta’s second drive for an easy interception. Anzalone then took the ball away two Penix throws later by, again, simply standing in the throwing lane. Penix wasn’t seeing the field and nothing changed as the game went on. He threw two more interceptions and had several other passes that could have been caught by the Bucs. Even his best play, a 76-yard toss to Jahan Dotson, was a throw into double coverage where two Bucs defensive backs collided, leaving Dotson wide open at the last second. This looked like an homage to Cooper Rush’s two catastrophic starts to open the season. Penix should rebound in Week 9 versus the Bengals, but his fantasy stock is undoubtedly on the decline. He is shuffling to the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 9.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs had 23 rushes for 153 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 8 win against the Vikings, adding two catches for 15 yards.
item.description:
Jahmyr Gibbs DET Running Back

Like all Minnesota opponents this season, the Lions got nothing going through the air. They resorted to a run-heavy game plan and shredded the Vikings defense on the ground for 228 yards. The rushing attack was led by Gibbs, who popped a handful of chunk runs in the second half after the Lions had mostly given up on attacking the Vikings through the air. This is Gibbs’ third 100-yard rushing effort of the 2026 season. His centrality in the Detroit offense makes Gibbs an elite play every week. He’ll take on the Dolphins in Week 9.

item.title: DJ Turner (ankle) was ruled out in Week 8 against the Titans.
item.description:
DJ Turner CIN Cornerback

Turner went down with an apparent ankle injury at the start of the fourth quarter. He was quickly ruled out, indicating the injury is major enough to put his status in question beyond this week. Josh Newton entered the game for Turner and allowed a go-ahead touchdown. Drake London will be set up for a nice fantasy WR1 game in Week 9 against the Bengals if Turner misses time.

item.title: Bakery Mayfield completed 0-of-3 passes for zero yards in the Bucs’ 16-0, Week 8 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

You read that correctly. Mayfield did not complete a pass and the Bucs handily defeated Atlanta. Playing in a torrential downpour, Tampa Bay’s defense eviscerated Michael Penix and the Bucs simply took the air out of the ball for four quarters. Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell combined for 310 yards on 52 carries. There was simply no need for Mayfield to handle the football outside of transferring it from the center to a running back. Mayfield did have a long touchdown to Ted Hurst that was knocked out of the rookie’s hand. This is just the second time a team has completed zero passes in the Super Bowl era and the first such game in over 50 years. Needless to say, Mayfield’s numbers will rebound in Week 9 when he takes on the Bears. He will be in the QB2 mix for that contest.

item.title: Jack Campbell was carted off in Week 8 with an apparent neck injury.
item.description:
Jack Campbell DET Linebacker

Campbell’s neck bent awkwardly on a tackle in the fourth quarter. He immediately went limp, and after more than ten minutes, he was carted off with what appeared to be a neck injury. The standout linebacker could be looking at an extended absence. We will update his status as we get more information.

item.title: Chargers declared CB Donte Jackson, CB Rodney Shelley, DB Deane Leonard, G Kayode Awosika, WR Theo Wease, and WR Brenen Thompson inactive for Week 8 against the Rams.
item.description:
Donte Jackson LAC Cornerback

Jackson, who was questionable headed into Sunday, will miss this game with a hamstring injury he suffered before the team’s Week 7 bye. The Bolts will also be without Derwin James, who was recently placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. The Chargers defense is beat up headed into this matchup with Matthew Stafford and the Rams.

Source: Chargers.com

item.title: Chiefs declared CB Mansoor Delane, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and DE Tyreke Smith inactive for Week 8 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Mansoor Delane KC Cornerback

Delane was initially listed as questionable for Week 8 on Friday. He was then ruled out over the weekend. Rookie EDGE R Mason Thomas was questionable for personal reasons but is active.

item.title: Jacoby Brissett completed 10-of-23 passes for 119 yards and an interception before being benched for Gardner Minshew in the third quarter.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett ARI Quarterback

He took four sacks, including back-to-back sacks to kill a third-quarter drive, before being replaced. Brissett hasn’t necessarily played this poorly all season, but we’d been getting plenty of questions at press conferences about if he’d remain the starter so we’re ultimately unsurprised by this move. Minshew took over and we assume Carson Beck will also be mentioned ahead of Week 9. Full Mike LaFleur press conference coverage to come, naturally.

item.title: JuJu Brents (neck/concussion) is active for Week 8 against the Patriots.
item.description:
JuJu Brents MIA Cornerback

Brents clears the NFL’s concussion protocol in time to take the field against the Patriots this week. The Dolphins declared OL Kadyn Proctor, TE Justin Joly, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., CB Jaylin Simpson, OG Christian Haynes, WR Jared Wayne and EDGE Jamree Kromah inactive for Week 8 against the Patriots. Losing Proctor, their starting left guard, is unfortunate.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Carlton Davis (neck) is active for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

The Patriots’ No. 2 perimeter cornerback makes his return from a multi-week neck injury for this divisional showdown. The Patriots declared CB Karon Prunty, S Elliott Davison, CB Channing Canada, QB Behren Morton, RB TreVeyon Henderson and WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) inactive for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Prunty and Canada have also missed multiple games, dealing with hamstring injuries. They are the Patriots’ primary backups on the perimeter. Both players practiced in full this week, so their absence is a little surprising.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Tyler Huntley (toe) will not return in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Tyler Huntley BAL Quarterback

Emergency QB3 Joe Fagnano will finish this one out after Huntley was ruled out during halftime. The Ravens’ QB2 completed 2-of-4 passes for zero yards in relief of Lamar Jackson, who exited after the first play of the game due to a thumb injury.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Left tackle Garrett Boles and EDGE Zach Allen are also active. All Broncos players who were questionable for Week 8 are active. After a disappointing two months to start the year, Waddle is at the back of the WR3 ranks for Week 8. Inactive for the Broncos are S Talana Hufanga, QB Sam Ehlinger, OL Gavin Ortega, DL Jordan Jackson, DL Tyler Oneydim, OL Kage Casey, and TE Dallen Bentley.

item.title: FOX’s Pam Oliver reports Zonovan Knight (head) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and won’t return.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

She got word from Mike LaFleur that Knight would be out. Knight wasn’t officially given an injury declaration as of yet, but it was a fairly textbook shoulder-to-the-head that caused a fumble towards the waning moments of the second half. Knight had 18 total yards on three carries and one catch before leaving. We would be surprised, given how brutal the hit he took looked, if he were available for Week 9. This leaves Tyler Allgeier as the lone healthy back for the second half of this game.

item.title: Brian Branch left Week 8’s game against the Vikings with an apparent head injury.
item.description:
Brian Branch DET Defensive Back

Branch tried to spear a Vikings ball carrier with his helmet but hit teammate DJ Wonnum in the head. Wonnum was later carted off with a head injury and Branch was able to leave to field under his own power. It would be a surprise if Branch returned to the ballgame.

Source: Pro Football Talk

item.title: FOX’s Pam Oliver reports Kendrick Bourne suffered a high-ankle sprain in Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Kendrick Bourne ARI Wide Receiver

Bourne limped to the sideline and later the locker room with trainers in a sequence towards the end of the half where the Cardinals lost three offensive skill players in just four plays. Bourne had a 29-yard catch before exiting. It seems likely he’ll miss multiple weeks and perhaps be a candidate for injured reserve.

item.title: Bucs EDGE Yaya Diaby suffered a knee injury in Week 8 against the Falcons and will not return.
item.description:
Yaya Diaby TB Outside Linebacker

Diaby went down in the first half and was ruled out before halftime. He was off to a slow start to the season before erupting for three sacks versus the Panthers last week. Diaby has started all eight Bucs games this year and has logged a snap share just under 60 percent.

item.title: Marcus Harris (ankle) is questionable to return Week 8 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Marcus Harris TEN Cornerback

Harris suffered an ankle injury and limped off the field with trainers in the first half of the Titans’ Week 8 game against the Bengals. He spent time in the blue tent and was subsequently carted to the locker room. Harris is questionable to return.

item.title: Tyler Huntley (toe) questionable to return in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Tyler Huntley BAL Quarterback

Huntley suffered a toe injury on a sack/fumble in the second quarter and was replaced by emergency QB3 Joe Fagnano. Huntley is eligible to return to the game if the team clears him to do so, despite some initial confusion that he would be unable to return after the Ravens were forced to put in their emergency QB.

item.title: Jaguars DT DaVon Hamilton suffered a knee injury in Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts and will not return.
item.description:
DaVon Hamilton

Hamilton got rolled up in ugly fashion in the second quarter and required the assistance of a cart. He was then quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game. That, it goes without saying, is never a good sign. It’s a huge loss for the Jags’ stout defense up front, as seventh-year pro Hamilton has been arguably having his best season.

item.title: Cade Mays (ankle) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

Mays went down with the injury in the second quarter. His absence will make it even tougher for the Detroit offense to navigate the Vikings’ complex blitzing schemes. Mays has dealt with injuries for much of the past month.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) left Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

His right ankle was rolled up on at the end of a running play and Love immediately slammed his helmet after walking off. He later went to the locker room with trainers and then was officially dubbed questionable. Not great. Love finished with nine carries for 23 yards, including a fourth-and-1 go at the goalline that he didn’t convert. We’ll see what reports say after the game but given Love has already missed time with ankle injuries this year, it’s hard to be optimistic about his status for next week.

item.title: Jaguars S Eric Murray suffered an elbow injury in Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts and will not return.
item.description:
Eric Murray

Veteran Murray went down early and was ruled out in the first half. It leaves the Jags’ safety depth perilously low.

Source: John Oehser

item.title: Lamar Jackson (thumb) will not return in Week 8’s game against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Jackson’s day officially ends after one play. The two-time MVP injured the thumb on his throwing hand on his first and only dropback of the day and immediately went to the locker room. The urgency with which Jackson was ushered from the field, coupled with how quickly he was ruled out, suggests this could be a serious enough injury that will result in another multi-game absence for Jackson. Tyler Huntley will be under center for the remainder of Week 8’s game against the Bills.

item.title: Jake Ferguson (ankle) left Dallas’ Week 8 game against the Cardinals and is questionable to return.
item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

He left in the first quarter. Hopefully his trendlines discouraged you from starting him, if not, we’re afraid it might be a zero for you. He was spotted on the sideline walking off.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (thumb) is questionable to return in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Shortly after he exited the field the team announced that Jackson was questionable to return after suffering a thumb injury on his throwing hand. Tyler Huntley immediately took over for Jackson, as the Ravens’ offense went three-and-out on their first drive of the game.

item.title: Deshaun Watson cleared concussion evaluation and is back in the game in Week 8 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson was evaluated after taking a hit to the head on the first drive. Shedeur Sanders played the end of the first drive, which ended in a Browns fumble, and now Watson is back in the game.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (hand) exited in the first quarter of Week 8’s game against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Jackson dropped back to pass on the Ravens’ first offensive play of the game and immediately headed for the sideline after hitting his hand on Bills LB Greg Rousseau. The injury was to Jackson’s throwing hand and appeared to be to his thumb, judging by what we could see on slow-motion replay. Trainers covered Jackson’s hand with a towel and immediately ushered him to the locker room. We will check back in when we receive more information on his status.

item.title: Deshaun Watson is being evaluated for a concussion in Week 8 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson was sacked on the second play of the game and then hit as he threw on the next play. The facemask of Steelers defender Jaquan Brisker hit the side of Watson’s helmet, and Watson was pulled into the blue tent for evaluation.

Source: Daniel Ayefusi

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “wouldn’t be surprised” if the Chiefs trade for a wide receiver.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Rapoport then named Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. as players to keep an eye on. Both wideouts are in the midst of down years and their teams have already leaked that they are on the trade block. Thomas Jr. would hopefully unlock the once-vaunted Patrick Mahomes deep ball. Downs, on the other hand, would be another underneath weapon for a passing attack that his simply asking too much of Rashee Rice right now. Both players’ fantasy stock would skyrocket via a trade.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Avieon Terrell (illness) is active for Week 8 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Avieon Terrell ATL Cornerback

Starting linebacker Divine Deablo is out with a forearm injury. Terrell, the No. 48 overall pick, made his first start in Week 6 before missing the following game with a groin issue. Also inactive for the Falcons are S Billy Bowman, QB Andy Dalton, LB Drake Jackson, CB Robert Longerbeam, RB Brian Robinson, QB Jack Strand.

item.title: Anthony Gould (concussion) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 8 game against the Jaguars.
item.description:
Anthony Gould IND Wide Receiver

The biggest news for fantasy purposes with the Colts inactives is simply that Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs are up, but that isn’t exactly surprising. Gould practiced in full the last two days of the week before being ruled out and stands a chance at being ready for Week 8. Inactive for the Colts are: LB Bryce Boettcher (groin), TE Pharaoh Brown, DT Kevin Givens, T Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback) and CB Justin Walley (knee).

item.title: Ben Skowronek (calf) is inactive for Week 8 against the Browns.
item.description:
Ben Skowronek PIT Wide Receiver

Steelers declared WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Brandin Echols, RB Eli Heidenreich, and CB Doneiko Slaughter inactive for Week 8 against the Browns. Skowronek will miss this game with a calf injury while Echols and Slaughter deal with hamstring injuries. Howard will serve as the emergency third quarterback.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid is active for the Bills’ Week 8 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

It was reported shortly before inactives were announced that Kincaid was expected to play. Now that he’s officially active, he will join DJ Moore, who is returning from a shoulder injury, to face a stingy Ravens defense. Despite some highly volatile performances this season, Kincaid will be in the TE1 mix this week.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is active for Jacksonville’s Week 8 game against the Colts.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

As expected based on the morning reporting. Meyers can be trusted as a WR4/FLEX mix against the Colts. Inactive for the Jaguars are S Antonio Johnson (knee), WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, LB Jamal Hill, DE Wesley Williams and DT Albert Regis.

item.title: Olamide Zaccheus (shoulder) is active for Week 8 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Olamide Zaccheaus ATL Wide Receiver

Zaccheus and Zachariah Branch will split the WR3 duties for Atlanta today. Neither player is on the fantasy radar for Week 8.

item.title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, WR Mitch Tinsley, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 8 against the Titans.
item.description:
Kyle Dugger CIN Safety

Dugger is ruled out after not practicing all week due to a quad injury. The rest of the Bengals’ inactives consist of healthy scratches and they enter Week 8 against the Titans with a relatively clean bill of health.

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) is active for the Bills’ Week 8 game against the Ravens.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid are both officially active, giving the Bills two of their top playmakers in what projects as one of the best matchups of the Week 8 slate against the Ravens. Moore returns for his first game since Week 4 and has caught 12 passes for 178 yards and one touchdown on 19 targets. He’ll profile as a fringe WR1/WR2 at home. The Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, CB Dee Alford, S Jalon Kilgore, LB Mike Danna, OG Ar’maj Reed-Adams, OT Spencer Brown, and DL Greg Gaines inactive for Week 8.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Max Melton (knee) is active for Arizona’s Week 8 game against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Max Melton ARI Cornerback

Melton is one of three questionables for the Cardinals that will suit up on Sunday, along with Hjalte Froholdt (knee) and Andrew Wingard (knee). Walter Nolen (ankle) and Jon Gaines (ankle/knee) were ruled out on Friday. Also inactive for the Cardinals are QB Carson Beck (emergency 3rd QB), OL Albert Reese, CB Starling Thomas V, RB Evan Hull and LB Eku Leota.

item.title: Raiders WR Jack Bech (forearm) is active for Week 8 against the Jets.
item.description:
Jack Bech LV Wide Receiver

Coming off injured reserve, Bech is active for the first time since Week 3. He was a small part of the offense before going down, but with this new coaching staff in evaluation mode, perhaps he will see more work down the stretch. He is nevertheless currently off the radar in 12-team leagues. Inactive for the Silver and Black are WR Dont’e Thornton Jr., WR Malik Benson, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, OG Bryce Cabeldue, DT JJ Pegues and QB Aidan O’Connell.

item.title: Aaron Jones (knee) is active for Week 8 against the Lions.
item.description:
Aaron Jones MIN Running Back

Jones was able to practice in full on Friday after battling the lingering knee issue all week. He could be somewhat limited against Detroit, creating a potentially bigger workload for Jordan Mason, who profiles as a flex option in 12-team leagues. Vikings declared Jakobe Thomas, Charles Demmings, Demond Claiborne, Caleb Tiernan, Elijah Williams, and Max Brosmer inactive against the Lions.

Source: Ben Goessling

item.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

Ridley entered the week questionable due to a hip injury but will be active after getting in a full practice on Friday. The Titans declared WR Carnell Tate, RB Tyjae Spears, P Tommy Townsend, CB Jaylon Jones, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, and DT Jackie Marshall inactive for Week 8 against the Bengals. Ridley will be one of the Titans’ top pass-catchers with Carnell Tate (shoulder) already ruled out, but is not more than a touchdown-dependent fantasy WR4 this week.

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is active for Week 8 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Right tackle Luke Goedeke is also active. Gainwell will continue mixing in behind Bucky Irving this week. He has yet to hit a dozen fantasy points in a game this year and there’s no reason to expect that to change anytime soon. Gainwell is a low-end RB4 for Week 8. Inactive for the Bucs are DL DeMonte Capehart, WR Emeka Egbuka, CB Ayden Garnes, OT Luke Haggard, and OG Billy Schrauth.

item.title: Ravens declared WR Elija Sarratt FS Jaylinn Hawkins, CB Chandler Rivers, OG Emery Jones, OG Vega Ioane, DT Aeneas Peebles, and QB Joe Fagnano inactive for Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Vega Ioane BAL Guard

The Ravens will be without rookie guard Vega Ioane, who suffered a knee injury in last week’s loss to the Bengals. While it’s yet another blow to an already banged-up offensive line, the Ravens do have Lamar Jackson returning from his three-game absence after he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 4. Hopefully, Jackson’s return can provide a much-needed spark to an offense that has managed just 23 points combined in its last two games.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Breece Hall (quad) is inactive for Week 8 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Hall seems to have suffered a rather serious setback with the quad injury that has been dogging him since September. This is easily said in hindsight, but it would seem Gang Green did not handle the issue particularly well. Hall is supposedly “hoping for next week,” but we would consider him on the wrong side of questionable until further notice. Isaiah Davis will serve as Braelon Allen’s breather back. Joining Hall on the shelf are EDGE David Bailey, WR Tim Patrick, CB Nahshon Wright, ED David Bailey, OL Kohl Levao and OL Max Mitchell.

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) is active for Dallas’ Week 8 game against the Cardinals.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens was expected to play after being listed as questionable. He can be counted on as a WR2 against a rough Cardinals defense. Inactive for the Cowboys are: WR KaVontae Turpin (rib), LB Dee Winters (Achilles), TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin), CB Shavon Revel Jr., OLB Tyrus Wheat and OT Drew Shelton. Winters and Turpin were ruled out on Friday, Schoonmaker was questionable. Also playing off questionable tags are DT Kenny Clark (bakc) and DT Jonathan Bullard (calf).

item.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Dalton Kincaid (chest) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid got banged up late in Week 6 and then got a bye week to rest up. He was limited in all three practices this week before being listed as questionable for Week 8. Kincaid will play a part-time role, per usual, but his elite efficiency has been enough to keep him in the TE1 mix so far. Playing in a shootout with the Ravens, he’ll remain in the top 12 tight ends this week as well.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe said Lamar Jackson (ankle) “won’t be 100 percent” in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

The good news, per Wolfe, is that Jackson will still be able to move despite playing on a bum ankle. Jackson told reporters the pain is “bearable” earlier in the week, which didn’t exactly inspire confidence from Ravens fans and fantasy managers. On the other hand, if Jackson is out there, we expect him to be mobile enough to lead a top-flight offense. A date with the Bills, which features the highest game total of the week, should also create an incredible environment for fantasy production. He is back at the top of the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Bills.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Colts want a third-round pick for Josh Downs.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

The Colts are already the league’s biggest sellers ahead of the trade deadline and they’re not done yet. While they get plenty of interest in Downs, a third-round pick might be too much to ask after his slow start to the year. Downs has 26 catches for 307 yards as we approach the midway point of the season. Downs is also set to become a free agent in the spring, meaning that he might play only a handful of games for his new team. On the other hand, his disappointing season can largely be written off as the product of a failing offense. Fantasy managers should at least hold onto Downs until the trade deadline, even if he’s barely a WR3 as things stand right now.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jordan Schultz reports the Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are amongst the teams that have “checked in” on a potential Jonathan Taylor trade.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

The Vikings dots have been getting connected for a while now, so it’s not surprising to see something of a confirmation they are interested. The Giants and Bengals also make all the sense in the world. Green Bay would be a fit, as well, though it would be a bit surprising to see the Broncos add to their running back surplus. Taylor, of course, would blow their other backs out of the water. There’s enough smoke here to believe a fire might break out, but the Colts can probably be taken at their word that it would take an overpay to pry away what amounts to their franchise player right now.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports DJ Moore (shoulder) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Ravens.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

Moore missed the Bills’ previous two games but had the bye week to get healthy. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. He’s likely still not at full strength, but fantasy managers can’t be too concerned given the game environment. The Bills’ matchup with Baltimore has all of the makings of a shootout. Moore was also operating as Josh Allen’s clear No. 1 receiver before aggravating his shoulder injury. Moore is a strong WR2 option for Week 8.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Micah Parsons (knee) is targeting a Week 12 return.
item.description:
Micah Parsons GB Defensive End

Parsons is still working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered late in the 2025 season. Per Rapoport, Parsons is expected to return to practice this week, meaning he will be designated to return from injured reserve in the coming days. He will then ramp up for a few weeks before hopefully returning in Week 12 against the Rams. Green Bay’s Week 11 bye will give him some extra time to get fully up to speed.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Josh Jacobs is “going to continue to play, but it is possible that he gets a suspension” at the end of the league’s investigation into several claims of domestic violence against him.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

A public records request revealed three additional accusations of domestic violence against Jacobs over the weekend. That is on top of the initial incident in which Jacobs ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property. The NFL put out a statement saying they will continue to look into Jacobs’ situation. Even though Jacobs was removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt List two weeks ago, the league’s investigation was still ongoing. Rapoport notes that the league is also looking into whether Jacobs was “upfront” with them about his disturbing legal situation. Of note, Jacobs’ team pushed to have video of the most recent incident sealed from public access while the league actively sought to have it released. Rapoport makes it sound like it may take some time for a suspension to be announced, but it’s more likely than not that Jacobs is suspended because of the most recent revelations.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jakobi Meyers (ankle/hamstring) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

Meyers was limited in the Jags’ first two practices of the week before being downgraded to a DNP on Friday. The team listed him as questionable, though the DNP was likely maintenance in hindsight. Meyers has topped three catches or 50 yards in just two games this year. He did, however, see 10 targets in the Jags’ Week 6 loss to the Texans before their bye. Meyers is in the WR4 mix for Week 8.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Kenneth Gainwell (hip) is “good to go” for Week 8 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Week 7 was Gainwell’s first game with more than seven touches all year. He handled 14 opportunities, all of which were carries, and they came in a 30-point blowout win over the Panthers. Unless the Bucs stay hot and roll over the Falcons, expect Gainwell’s touch total to return to the single digits. He is barely in the RB4 mix for Week 8.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Breece Hall (quad) is “hoping for next week.”
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported an hour ago that Braelon Allen will get the start, but he didn’t explicitly rule out Hall for Week 8. Fowler’s report makes things relatively black and white. Hall will miss today’s game versus the Raiders. He got in three practices this week before being listed as questionable on Friday. Though a Week 9 return is on the table, the Jets’ failure to put Hall on IR, only for him to miss at least five games, suggests his injury is worse than they initially expected. It’s possible he’s held out beyond today’s game. Braelon Allen will continue to dominate the Jets’ backfield touches until Hall returns.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Treylon Burks (foot) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks was limited in Friday’s practice before being listed as questionable. With Terry McLaurin done for the year, Burks is one of several role players for the Commanders who will be asked to step up in the back half of 2026. Burks has nine catches for 152 yards and two scores in five appearances this year.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts “would seek a similar compensation package” to the Christian McCaffrey trade for Jonathan Taylor.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

The Panthers netted second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round picks for McCaffrey when they sent him to San Francisco in 2022. Indy reportedly turned down an offer of a second-round selection plus another pick for Taylor, meaning they have their eyes set on the full compensation that Carolina landed. The fact that the Colts abruptly changed their stance on trading Taylor at all this weekend suggests it’s only a matter of time before a deal gets done. They have until November 10th, the Tuesday after Week 9, to find a trade partner.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Braelon Allen is expected to start for the Jets in Week 8 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Braelon Allen NYJ Running Back

Rapoport mentioned that Breece Hall is still dealing with his quad injury, though he didn’t explicitly say that Hall will not play this week. For now, fantasy managers should assume he is out, marking his fifth absence because of the injury. Allen is averaging 20.8 touches and 105 yards from scrimmage without Hall this year. He is back on the RB1/2 border for Week 8.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Browns declared QB Dillon Gabriel, QB Taylen Green, LB Justin Jefferson, CB Noah Igbinoghene, RB Audric Estime, and C Parker Brailsford inactive for Week 8 against the Steelers.
item.description:
Dillon Gabriel CLE Quarterback

Gabriel was activated off of injured reserve at the beginning of the week and will serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback ahead of rookie Taylen Green. The Browns enter Week 8 with a relatively healthy depth chart, making their inactives healthy scratches against the Steelers.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter named Calvin Ridley as a potential trade candidate.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

Schefter threw out several names, many of whom have already been bandied about as trade candidates. Among the lesser-discussed options, he included Jerry Jeudy and Jauan Jennings in addition to Ridley. All three are veteran wideouts who have simply disappeared in the current iterations of their respective offenses. Even with new landing spots in the cards for the trio, none of them are worth holding onto in standard fantasy leagues. Ridley has five catches for 81 yards this year. He is expected to play through his hip injury today.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Saquon Barkley “will not be traded before next week’s trade deadline.”
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Though teams can change their minds in very short periods of time, Rapoport’s wording on this matter is rather definitive. Sitting at 2-5 with Jalen Hurts out for the year, it makes sense for the Eagles to be sellers at the trade deadline. Players including Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Hollywood Brown have also been the subject of trade rumors. All three are more likely than Barkley to land with new teams over the next week. Barring a change of heart from GM Howie Roseman, Barkley will continue to be the focal point of a failing offense for the remainder of the season.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports George Pickens (hamstring/shoulder) is expected to play in Week 8 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens has been playing through the shoulder issue for a few weeks, but the hamstring was a new addition to his injury report. We suspect the hamstring injury is what earned him the questionable tag on Friday, though it’s a moot point now. Staring down a likely shootout with a weak Arizona defense, Pickens, even at less than full strength, is a locked-in WR2 for Week 8.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jaylen Waddle (chest) is “trending toward playing” in Week 8 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle suffered the chest injury late in the Broncos’ Week 7 win over the Cardinals and a doomed trick play. He was leveled by Josh Sweat several yards behind the line of scrimmage. The Broncos held him out of Wednesday’s practice before giving him two limited sessions and a questionable tag. Though we suspect he is on some form of a snap count, it looks like Waddle is giving it a go. Already struggling to put up WR3 fantasy numbers, we’re regarding him as a high-risk FLEX play versus Kansas City.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders plan to start Kirk Cousins “as long as possible.”
item.description:
Kirk Cousins LV Quarterback

Schefter added that the team does not feel their current four-game losing streak is the fault of Cousins. He threw for nine touchdowns in the first three games, all of which the Raiders won. Cousins has just seven touchdowns over his past four outings, though he has only thrown two interceptions and taken just five sacks during that stretch. The Raiders are probably right to lay the blame elsewhere. Still, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is waiting in the wings. He is the future of the franchise, and his time grows closer with every Raiders loss. Vegas takes on the Jets this week. They then get a gauntlet of San Francisco, Seattle, and Denver. A 0-3 run that late in the season would likely spell the end of Cousins as their starter.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders “currently have no plans” to trade Maxx Crosby.
item.description:
Maxx Crosby LV Defensive End

Crosby was the subject of rampant trade rumors as the deadline approached last year. Nothing materialized then, but the team ultimately found a partner in the Ravens during the offseason. The deal was signed and Crosby had his flight to Baltimore booked, but the Ravens backed out at the last minute after Crosby failed his physical. Crosby’s baulky knee was a long-term concern for the Ravens, though it hasn’t even been mentioned this year. Schefter added that Crosby no longer wants to be traded, which was not a foregone conclusion this time last year. Even in the midst of a four-game losing streak, the Raiders are still contenders in the AFC West, giving them reason enough to hold onto their star pass-rusher.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 8 against the Bears.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed reportedly avoided a major injury in the collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the end zone in Week 7, an injury that will claim at least one game from the veteran speedster. There’s not really a ton of fantasy value behind Smith-Njigba in Seattle, although veteran Cooper Kupp could see a target or two trickle his way in Shaheed’s absence.

item.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) is expected to be active for Week 8 against the Bears.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

The team has yet to activate Charbonnet from injured reserve but removed him from the injury report Saturday, leaving only the procedural step in the way of his season debut. He likely returns to a limited role as the team manages his reps in his first game since tearing his ACL in 2025. Rookie Jadarian price is also expected to play after being removed from the injury report. He, too, will need to be activated from injured reserve.

item.title: Seahawks removed Jadarian Price (chest) from the injury report Saturday and he is expected to play in Week 8 against the Bears.
item.description:
Jadarian Price SEA Running Back

The team has yet to activate him from injured reserve, a procedural move that is expected to come before they take the field in Week 8 against the Bears on Monday Night Football. Zach Charbonnet is also expected to be activated from injured reserve, giving the team their top two backs for the first time this season. No word yet on an expected snap count for either, although Price would seem to be in line to serve as the top option in the backfield considering it will be Charbonnet’s season debut.

item.title: Broncos placed RB RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
RJ Harvey DEN Running Back

Whoa, that escalated quickly. Harvey reportedly suffered a knee injury in practice this week that initially caused the Broncos to rule him out for Week 8, with the team then making the procedural move of placing him on injured reserve Saturday. Harvey will now miss the next four games, at minimum, as he rehabs the injury, leaving rookie Jonah Coleman and veteran J.K. Dobbins to handle primary backfield duties with Tyler Badie also on injured reserve. Coleman warrants weekly FLEX status, at minimum.

item.title: Chiefs placed CB L’Jarius Sneed (knee) on inured reserve.
item.description:
L'Jarius Sneed KC Cornerback

That was somewhat unexpected. Sneed missed Wednesday’s practice for personal reasons and was limited Thursday and Friday. He was moved to injured reserve a day later. The Chiefs are now down their top two corners after Mansoor Delane was ruled out for Week 8, creating a much softer matchup for the Broncos on Sunday.

item.title: Chargers placed S Derwin James (hamstring) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Derwin James LAC Safety

Previous reports indicated the team was considering a stint on injured reserve following an aggravation of his hamstring injury, with Saturday’s transaction confirming those suspicions.
